strategies.content: Structure the funding of receivable purchases through a multi-tiered funding stack, typically comprising proceeds from a senior revolving facility, variable loan notes (mezzanine), a subordinated revolving facility, and the recycling of collections received in respect of purchased receivables.

Utilize a Master Framework Agreement to centralize common definitions and interpretation principles, requiring all Transaction Documents to incorporate these provisions by reference to ensure consistency and reduce repetition across the transaction suite.

Include an express provision stating that principles of construction set out in the Master Framework Agreement apply automatically to any subsidiary instrument or deed that incorporates the Master Agreement by reference.

Draft a 'Multi-Capacity' clause ensuring that if a party acts in more than one role (e.g., Cash Manager and Account Bank), the agreement applies to them as if they were separate entities for each role, while waiving requirements for them to give notices to themselves.

Define 'Account Bank Eligible Institution' to accommodate both traditional authorized deposit-taking institutions (with minimum credit ratings) and Electronic Money Institutions (subject to specific approval or regulatory status), reflecting the diversity of potential account providers.

Establish comprehensive 'Account Bank Events' triggers for bank replacement, including insolvency (referencing specific regulations for E-Money institutions if applicable), loss of eligibility/downgrade, loss of regulatory authorization, or material breach/default under the specific account agreement.

Permit 'Agreed Ad Hoc Funding' from a subordinated lender to cover specific approved costs or expenses (excluding principal repayments) necessary to prevent Early Amortisation or Events of Default, subject to senior agent approval (not to be unreasonably withheld).

definitions.content: “ABS Transaction” means any securitisation of any Receivables originated by the Seller, which involves the marketing and distribution of securities in the public markets.

ABS Transaction Fee: means the fee payable to the Senior Lenders or Agent upon the voluntary cancellation or prepayment of the Senior Facility for the purposes of refinancing through an ABS Transactio...

“Acceding Swap Provider Minimum Rating” means, in relation to a new or successor Swap Provider that is not an affiliate of Swap Provider, a rating for its long-term unsecured and non-credit-enhanced debt obligations of A or higher by S&P or Fitch or A2 or higher by Moody’s.

Acceptance: means the formal confirmation by the Purchaser to the Seller accepting an Offer to sell Receivables, which effects the sale and transfer of such Receivables under the terms of the Receivab...

“Accession Date” means, in respect of any party, the date on which it accedes to:

if it is an acceding Senior Lender, the Senior Facility Agreement and the Master Framework Agreement, in accordance with clause 18 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Senior Facility Agreement;

if it is an acceding Mezzanine Note Purchaser or another member of a Mezzanine Note Purchaser Group, the Mezzanine Facility Agreement and the Master Framework Agreement, in accordance with clause 12 (Increase of the Mezzanine Commitments) or clause 13 (Assignments and Transfers) of the Mezzanine Facility Agreement; or

if is an acceding Swap Provider, in accordance with Clause 3.47 (Accession of a new or successor Swap Provider) of the Master Framework Agreement.

Account Acceleration Notice: means a notice in a form which is in all material respects the same as that set out in Exhibit A (Account Control Notice) of the Issuer Account Bank Agreement duly execute...
“Account Bank” means any Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as the context requires.
“Account Bank Downgrade” means, in respect of any Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, the point in time when it ceases to be an Account Bank Eligible Institution.

“Account Bank Eligible Institution” means any Issuer Account Bank, Collections Account Bank or any proposed Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as at any date of determination, that:

is and remains duly authorised in respect of its deposit taking activities under the laws of the jurisdiction in which it is operating; and

if it is not an Electronic Money Institution, maintains certain corporate ratings, which are short term unsecured, unguaranteed and unsubordinated debt obligations rated at least P-1 by Moody’s, A-l by S&P and F-1 by Fitch; or

if it is an Electronic Money Institution, is an Approved Electronic Money Institution.
“Account Mandate” means any account mandate (including any account terms and conditions) in relation to the Issuer Accounts or the Collections Account.

“Accounting Principles” means generally accepted accounting principles in England and Wales and/or the international financial reporting standards (IFRS) within the meaning of Regulation 1606/2002/EC (or as otherwise adopted or amended from time to time) or other generally accepted accounting principles, as applied by each relevant entity within the Seller Group for the purpose of its financial statements.

Accounting Reference Date: means the date on which the Issuer's financial year ends for accounting purposes, typically 31 December or such other date as specified in the Issuer's corporate representat...

“Acknowledgment of Collections Account Declaration of Trust” means an acknowledgment of the creation of a trust over a Collections Account substantially in the form set out in a Collections Account Declaration of Trust.

“Adjusted Loan Terms” means, in respect of any Receivable and its related Consumer Loan, that it has been originated in circumstances in which the Borrower had originally specified an amount of borrowing and term of the loan at the time the Borrower applied for the Consumer Loan and the Seller subsequently offered to that Borrower an option to adjust the loan terms by increasing or decreasing the amount of borrowing and/or the term of the proposed Consumer Loan and the Borrower consequently adjusted the terms of their initial application.

Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers Excess Concentration Amount: means the amount by which the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Receivables related to Prime Borrowers with Adjusted Loan Term...
“Affected Person” means the Facility Agent, the Security Trustee, any Senior Lender, any Mezzanine Note Purchaser, any Mezzanine Funding Agent and any Swap Provider.

Affected Person Tax Credit: means any credit against, relief or remission for, or repayment of, any Tax obtained by an Affected Person (or any of its Affiliates) that is attributable to a Tax Deductio...

“Affiliate” or “affiliate” means, in respect of any Person, any other Person that, directly or indirectly, is in control of, is controlled by or is under common control with, that Person or is a director or officer of that Person.

After Tax Basis: means that a payment is to be made in an amount which, after deduction of all Taxes required to be paid by the recipient in respect of the receipt of such amount, leaves the recipient...
“Agency Fee Letter” means the fee letter dated on or about the Signing Date between the Issuer, the Facility Agent and the Security Trustee.

“Agreed Ad Hoc Funding Amount” means, as at any Cut-Off Date, any Subordinated Advances made by the Subordinated Lender to fund specified ad hoc costs payable by the Issuer in accordance with the Transaction Documents which are pre-approved in writing by the Facility Agent (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed (including, but not limited to, situations where withholding consent would result in not being able to prevent the occurrence of, or allow the remediation of, an Early Amortisation Event or an Event of Default)) or any other costs and expenses (but not principal repayment amounts or redemption amounts on the Senior Facility or Mezzanine Notes) specified in clauses 3.1 (d), (e) or (h) (Purpose) of the Subordinated Facility Agreement.

“Agreed Adjusted Ad Hoc Funding Amount” means, as at any Cut-Off Date, an amount equal to the higher of:

zero; and

an amount equal to:

the aggregate Agreed Ad Hoc Funding Amounts incurred from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date; and

the aggregate of the amounts calculated under paragraph (ii)(A)(2)(cc) of the definition of Subordinated Redemption Amount, from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date.
